title: Leek and Potato Soup
subtitle: Smooth, creamy vichyssoise-style leek and potato soup
excerpt: A smooth, silky soup of leeks and potatoes in a good stock, finished with cream and served hot or cold. One of the most elegant simple soups in the French and British canon.

recipe.sourceNotes: Leek and potato soup, in its elegant chilled form, is known as vichyssoise: a dish created by French chef Louis Diat at the Ritz-Carlton hotel in New York in 1917, inspired by a childhood memory of his mother cooling the family's leek and potato soup with cold cream and milk in summer. The name comes from the spa town of Vichy, near Diat's birthplace. The same soup served hot is a standard of both French bourgeois and British domestic cooking, where it requires no special name. The soup uses the white and pale green parts of the leek only: the dark green tops are too fibrous and intensely flavoured for a smooth, delicate result. Floury potatoes give a better, more velvety consistency than waxy potatoes, which can give a slightly gluey result when blended.

recipeTools.notes: A large saucepan for the soup.

content.text: Wash the leeks very thoroughly: grit between the layers is the most common problem with this soup. Split them lengthways and rinse under cold running water, fanning the layers. Use only the white and pale green parts. The soup blends most smoothly in a jug blender in small batches: do not fill the blender more than half full when blending a hot liquid. To serve cold as vichyssoise, blend, chill thoroughly, and add a little extra cream and salt before serving as the cold temperature mutes the seasoning.

items.preparation: white and pale green parts only, washed and sliced

content.text: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the leeks and onion and cook gently for 10 minutes until completely soft but not coloured. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.

Add the potatoes, stock, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes until the potatoes are completely tender. Remove the bay leaf. Blend until completely smooth. Stir in the cream. Season.
Reheat gently if needed. Serve in warm bowls with a swirl of cream and a scatter of snipped chives.
